html:
The Ramaytush are the Ohlone people of the San Francisco Peninsula, in today's San Francisco and San Mateo counties. The name, from a word for the language they spoke, came into use in the 1970s and has since been taken up by their descendants. The people of the northern tip, where the city now stands, were the Yelamu.

They lived in small villages by the bay and the ocean, gathering shellfish, acorns and seeds, and fishing from boats of tule reeds. In 1776 Spain founded the presidio of San Francisco and Mission San Francisco de Asís (Mission Dolores) in their land. Within a generation disease and mission life had nearly destroyed them, and the survivors married into other groups. The California genocide after 1850 hit the remaining Native people of the region. Across the Golden Gate lived the Coast Miwok.
